ECTIVE: To study sleep in stiff person syndrome (SPS) and stiff limb
ome (SLS). BACKGROUND: Muscle hyperactivity syndromes in-
the classic stiff person syndrome (SPS) and the stiff leg syndrome (a
ariant). Several neurophysiological investigations suggest an impair-
of GABA-ergic inhibitory circuits leading to hyperactivity of the alpha
opr neurons in the motor cortex, spinal cord and brainstem.
minobutyric acid is the major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central
yous system and it plays an essential role in the induction and mainte-
ce of sleep. DESIGN/METHODS: Five patients affected by SPS (3) and
(2) underwent a polygraphic monitoring using a 14-channel EEG ma-
for two consecutive night. Scalp electrodes were placed according to
10-20 International System. Polygraphic channels included ECG,
, and submental, left and right tibialis anterior and gastrocnemious
ie EMG. Sleep stages were spotted according to the standard criteria.
the time of the recording, all patients were not taking any drug. RE-
TS: Sleep pattern was similar in all patients and was characterized
: long sleep latency; total sleep time reduction; frequent awakenings and
IEG arousals; absence of stage 3 and 4 of NREMS; and REM sleep reduc-
on. These findings were not related to leg myoclonus and apnea presence,
dicating a disturbance of induction and maintenance of sleep similar to
changes produced by the GABA, receptor dysfunction. No differences in
G-sleep pattern were found with regard to the severity and duration of
disease and between SPS and SLS cases. This suggests an early in-
ement of both forebrain and GABA also in variants whose spasms and
rigidity of limbs mimic a spinal origin. CONCLUSIONS/RELEVANCE:
a abnormalities represent a further evidence of a dysfunction of GABA-
ergic inhibitory system in muscle hyperactivity syndromes.
